glosses: A container, typically made of glass or plastic and having a tapered neck, used primarily for holding liquids.

examples.text: Beer is often sold in bottles.
He had one hand on the bounce bottle—and he’d never let go of that since he got back to the table—but he had a handkerchief in the other and was swabbing his deadlights with it.

glosses: The contents of such a container.

examples.text: I only drank a bottle of beer.

glosses: A container with a rubber nipple used for giving liquids to infants, a baby bottle.

examples.text: The baby wants a bottle.
With Marvin getting older ... and walking now ... I thought it was time to start weaning him off of his bottle.

glosses: (originally \"bottle and glass\" as rhyming slang for \"arse\") Nerve, courage.

examples.text: You don’t have the bottle to do that!
He was going to ask her out, but he lost his bottle when he saw her.

glosses: A container of hair dye, hence with one’s hair color produced by dyeing.

examples.text: Did you know he’s a bottle brunette? His natural hair color is strawberry blonde.

glosses: Intoxicating liquor; alcohol.

examples.text: to drown one’s troubles in the bottle
to hit the bottle
See that black boy over there runnin' scared / His ol' man's in a bottle / He done quit his 9 to 5 to drink full time / So now he's livin' in the bottle.

glosses: To seal (a liquid) into a bottle for later consumption. Also fig.

examples.text: This plant bottles vast quantities of spring water every day.

The temptation is to regard him [John Ogdon] as an idiot savant, a big talent bottled inside a recalcitrant body and accompanied by a personality that seems not just unremarkable, but almost entirely blank.

glosses: To feed (an infant) baby formula.

examples.text: Because of complications she can't breast feed her baby and so she bottles him.

glosses: To refrain from doing (something) at the last moment because of a sudden loss of courage.

examples.text: The rider bottled the big jump.

glosses: To throw away a leading position.

examples.text: Arsenal bottled the Premier League.

glosses: To strike (someone) with a bottle.

examples.text: He was bottled at a nightclub and had to have facial surgery.

glosses: To pelt (a musical act on stage, etc.) with bottles as a sign of disapproval.

examples.text: Meat Loaf was once bottled at Reading Festival.

glosses: Of pages printed several on a sheet: to rotate slightly when the sheet is folded two or more times.

examples.text: Closely related to creep is the process of bottling. As you may have noticed from your folded sheet of paper, pages don't merely creep when they're folded — they also rotate slightly. This rotation or bottling is caused by the thickness or bulk of the paper.
